images.title: Why is AI bad at math?
images.subtitle: Chatbots estimate sums like a shopkeeper. A calculator adds them exactly.

images.title: A chatbot is the shopkeeper, not the till

pairs.left: Glances at a basket and says about forty dollars
pairs.right: Writes the answer that looks most likely

pairs.left: Learned from thousands of till receipts
pairs.right: Learned from huge amounts of text
Often right, sometimes wrong in a few digits

pairs.left: The till adds every price, exactly
pairs.right: A calculator or code tool computes exactly

images.note: Unlike a shopkeeper, a chatbot does not say when it is guessing.

images.title: Numbers are cut where the rule says, not where you would

items.label: You type 48172
items.text: To a person it is 48 thousand and 172.

items.label: Tokenizer cuts it
items.text: Groups of up to three digits from the left: 481 and 72.

items.label: Model reads chunks
items.text: The chunk 481 mixes thousands and hundreds.

items.label: Answer is written
items.text: Digits are predicted as text, one piece at a time.

images.note: Some models cut numbers into single digits instead.

images.title: Let a tool do the adding

columns.heading: Ask for the answer
items: The model predicts digits as text
Close in size, maybe wrong in the middle

columns.heading: Ask for a calculation run
items: The model writes the sum as code
A tool runs it and returns the result
You can see the code and check it

images.verdict: For figures that matter, let the model explain and the tool compute.
